profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the engineering lead for an internal developer-platform initiative and the analytics engineer supporting the same effort at a mid-sized SaaS company. The company is preparing a Q2 internal report on how LLM-assisted tools changed team collaboration in software development, drawing on a pilot of an AI code assistant, an AI documentation bot, a team survey, usage telemetry, and two case studies from product teams. The immediate need is to align interfaces and handoffs for the evidence package that will feed both an executive rollout memo and an internal engineering wiki page. The agenda is to confirm what each person will deliver, which version of the pilot data will be used, what should count as 'team-level impact' in the writeup, and what 'Friday handoff' means for the shared deadline. The expected outcome is apparent agreement that the engineering lead will assemble the narrative and case studies while the analytics engineer will provide the survey output, pilot dataset, and collaboration-impact analysis in time for the report draft.

members.name: Priya Raman
members.expertise: Developer tooling rollouts, engineering documentation, adoption programs, cross-team coordination
members.background: Priya leads the internal developer-experience workstream and has previously driven adoption of CI/CD and code-search platforms across several product groups; she is used to packaging technical pilots into concise narratives for engineering leadership.
members.private_state: Priya wants the report to read as a clean, decision-ready story that supports broader rollout of the LLM tooling, and she is trying to avoid last-minute churn caused by overly detailed analytical artifacts that non-analysts will not consume.
hidden_assumptions: When someone asks for 'survey results' in a coordination context, they usually mean a presentation-ready output such as a few summary slides or a compact chart/table export that can be dropped straight into a memo.
The phrase 'the pilot dataset' refers to the cleaned combined table already used in earlier internal updates, limited to the two featured product teams and excluding light-touch trial users.
A 'team-level impact' section is valid if each participating team has a single clear summary of collaboration changes, even when role-level differences are not shown separately.
A 'Friday handoff' means by end of business Friday Pacific Time, because that is how internal launch-readiness deliverables are normally scheduled.

members.name: Evan Morales
members.expertise: Telemetry pipelines, survey analysis, metric lineage, mixed-method evidence packaging
members.background: Evan supports internal platform and product initiatives with instrumentation, survey analysis, and reproducible reporting; he previously worked on experimentation infrastructure and is attentive to traceability and reuse of analytical outputs.
members.private_state: Evan wants the evidence package to remain analytically defensible and reusable for later benchmarking or publication, and he is concerned about informal handoffs that make the numbers hard to reproduce or reinterpret.
hidden_assumptions: When a partner requests 'survey results,' the most useful handoff is the working analytical surface itself, such as a notebook output or dashboard link with filters, rather than only static summary slides.
The phrase 'the pilot dataset' refers to the canonical source export covering all instrumented pilot users during the study window, from which later exclusions and featured subsets can be derived.

A credible 'team-level impact' analysis for collaboration should preserve subgroup structure such as engineers, QA, and PMs within each team, because collaboration effects can be misleading when collapsed.
A 'Friday handoff' means the package is available by Friday 5 PM Central European Time so colleagues in Dublin and Berlin can pick it up before their weekend.

misalignment_points.topic: What form the survey results will take
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree that Evan will send the 'survey results' for Priya to fold into the report.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya expects a presentation-ready artifact: a few polished charts, headline percentages, and selected quotes in a format she can quickly paste into the memo and wiki.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan expects to hand over an analytical surface: a notebook export or dashboard link with tabs, filters, and underlying response summaries that Priya can inspect or pull screenshots from.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both formats plausibly count as 'results,' and in cross-functional software teams people often use that phrase loosely without distinguishing between a consumable summary and an exploratory analysis artifact, so the agreement sounds complete.

misalignment_points.topic: Which dataset 'the pilot dataset' refers to
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to using 'the pilot dataset' when combining telemetry and case-study evidence.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means the already-cleaned combined table for the two highlighted product teams, with one-off trial users and partially instrumented accounts removed because that is the version leadership has already seen.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan means the canonical export for everyone in the pilot instrumentation window, including users later filtered out of narrative reporting, because any published subset should be derivable from that base.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There really is a well-known artifact informally called 'the pilot dataset,' but the name is used for different points in the data lineage; because both versions are legitimate and familiar, the label gives a false sense of specificity.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as showing team-level impact
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the report should highlight 'team-level impact' of the LLM tools on collaboration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya thinks this means one concise finding per team about whether collaboration improved overall, for example faster code-review turnaround or clearer handoffs, with role distinctions collapsed for readability.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan thinks this means the analysis must still show within-team subgroup differences, such as engineers reporting fewer interruptions while QA reports more review ambiguity, because otherwise the collaboration claim is too coarse.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both speakers sincerely endorse the same goal and use the same phrase, but the hidden difference is the evidentiary standard for when that phrase is satisfied, which usually stays implicit unless someone is explicitly challenged on methodology.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both confirm that the package will be handed off 'by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya assumes the materials will arrive by Friday end of day Pacific Time, leaving her Friday afternoon to consolidate the memo before sending it to leadership.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan assumes the materials need to be ready by Friday 5 PM Central European Time, because the research-program partners in Europe are part of the expected downstream audience and he treats their workday as the relevant cutoff.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Deadlines in distributed software organizations are often stated only as a weekday when everyone believes the context is obvious, and because both interpret 'Friday' as a reasonable professional deadline, neither thinks clarification is necessary.
